thesis: Avantor's Q2 2026 report (Jul 29) beat EPS consensus and lifted full-year adjusted EPS guidance, and the stock has kept trending since — now at its 52-week high and well above its 200-day average — which suggests the post-earnings re-rating is still being absorbed. The strongest counter-case is fundamental: a pending securities class action alleges Avantor misrepresented its competitive position and overstated VWR goodwill, and it is not resolved; Q3 results on Oct 28 are a pending binary event, so this caps at medium. No specific news explained Friday's 3.1x volume.
invalidation: Q3 results on Oct 28 miss or full-year guidance is cut, an adverse class-action development, or a close back below the 20-day average.
sources: Syfe (MT Newswires headline, Q2 lifts 2026 adjusted EPS outlook): https://www.syfe.com/stocks/us/AVTR

thesis: Varonis signed a definitive agreement (8-K, Oct 15, 2026) to be acquired by Proofpoint for $49.75 per share in cash, with committed Thoma Bravo financing and a close expected in 1H 2027. At $48.705 the stock is pinned about 2.1% below the deal price, so upside appears capped while a deal break would expose it to a large drop — an unfavorable setup for this strategy.
invalidation: A topping bid above $49.75 emerges, reopening upside.

thesis: Fervo is down 43% over 60 days to within 1% of its 52-week low, after its Aug 12 call disclosed an expected transmission shutdown curtailing Cape Station deliveries and an Oct 6 Morpheus Research report alleged undisclosed thermal decline, water loss and seismic equipment damage; several plaintiff firms have opened investigations. The curtailment is a confirmed company disclosure while the short-report claims are unrebutted allegations, which suggests continued risk rather than a recovery setup.
invalidation: The company rebuts the Morpheus findings with operating data and confirms a firm Cape Station transmission restoration timeline.

thesis: Netskope is up 32% over 60 days and above its 200-day average, but this run found no confirmed company catalyst for that move (the latest dated coverage is its June fiscal Q1 report), and Friday's 7.1% drop on 2.9x volume has no identified cause, so the evidence is unresolved. A March 2026 plaintiff-firm solicitation and the ongoing Fortinet patent litigation are narrative risks only.
invalidation: A confirmed company-specific catalyst (e.g. a guidance raise or major contract) that explains the trend.

thesis: SELLAS's value hinges on the pending final analysis of its Phase 3 REGAL trial (78 of 80 required events reported), an unresolved binary event; the stock fell 12% Friday on 2.8x volume with no identified news and is down 26% over 60 days. Shares outstanding rose from ~153M to ~197M via warrant exercises in 1H 2026, and a plaintiff firm is soliciting investors.

Sunstone raised its 2026 AFFO guidance with its Aug 6 Q2 report (asset sale, buybacks) and trades near its 52-week high, above its 200-day average. But the Oct 15-16 volume surge (4.2x) that triggered this review has no identified news and fell on monthly options-expiration Friday, so the signal reads as largely mechanical rather than a new fundamental catalyst, and the guidance raise is about 50 trading days old.
invalidation: Q3 results (around Nov 5-6) show RevPAR or AFFO below the raised guidance, or a close back below the 200-day average.

thesis: CCC signed a definitive agreement (announced Oct 15, 2026) to be acquired for cash by a GTCR-led group including Elliott at about $6.1B enterprise value, expected to close in Q1 2027 subject to stockholder and regulatory approval. Oct 15 volume of 324M shares and Friday's 0.7% range around $7.61 suggest the price is pinned to the deal terms, capping upside.

Wise reported fiscal Q2 2027 results after the Oct 15 close and fell 9.2% Friday on 2.7x volume; this run could not confirm what in the results drove the drop. A Brussels prosecutor inquiry disclosed Jun 1, 2026 remains open with no scheduled next step found, and the CEO faced an earlier FCA fit-and-proper probe. With the drop's cause unresolved there is no long read.
invalidation: Evidence the drop was non-fundamental (e.g. guidance intact) and the stock reclaims its pre-results level.

thesis: JFrog fell 10.8% Friday on 2.6x volume and sits about 20% below its Aug 28 52-week high; this run found no news explaining the drop (the latest identified items are a July Morgan Stanley downgrade and 2024-era plaintiff investigations). With the cause of the sell-off unidentified, the evidence is unresolved.
invalidation: An identified non-fundamental cause for the drop, or Q3 results that reaffirm guidance.

thesis: Caesars agreed on May 28, 2026 to be acquired by Fertitta Entertainment for $31.00 per share in cash (about $17.6B including debt), with committed financing and a shareholder vote set for Sep 22; gaming approvals across 16 states remain pending. At $28.80 the stock trades about 7.6% below the deal price — a merger-arbitrage spread reflecting regulatory timing risk, with upside capped at the deal price.
invalidation: Deal terms are raised, or the regulatory timeline shortens materially.

thesis: Northern Trust's 2.2x volume Friday came with a flat close on monthly options-expiration day, and this run found no company news behind it; Q3 2026 results are due in late October, an unresolved binary event. A former senior fiduciary advisor is accused of defrauding clients (suits seeking at least $35M; the bank says it reimbursed clients) — whether criminal charges are confirmed was not established, so it is narrative only.
invalidation: Q3 results show a clear fee/NII beat with a raised outlook.

thesis: Crescent Energy priced an 80M-share primary Class A common stock offering at $12.50 on Oct 8, 2026 (8-K; a KKR affiliate agreed to buy 40M shares), a completed dilutive raise; the stock then rose 10.1% Friday on 2.1x volume with no identified news. The new-share issuance is a dilution risk and the rally's driver is unconfirmed, so there is no long read.
invalidation: A disclosed accretive use of the offering proceeds (e.g. an acquisition) that explains the rally.
